If you die in Brazil with a Brazilian‑owned apartment, that property **automatically transfers to your heirs under Art. 1.784 of the Civil Code** [1]. The Brazilian inheritance regime applies only to assets located in Brazil. Your U.S. bank accounts are **not subject to Brazilian inheritance rules**; they remain under U.S. law.

**What the Brazilian rules mean for a foreign estate**

* Foreign heirs are treated like Brazilian citizens for succession purposes.  
* The estate is split into a *reserved portion* (at least **50 %** of the estate) that must go to the legal heirs and a *disposable portion* that the testator may distribute freely.  
* Inheritance tax (ITCMD) can reach up to **8 %** of the value of the inherited assets [2].

**U.S. estate implications**

* If the total value of your U.S.‑situated assets exceeds **$60 ,000**, your estate must file Form 706‑NA.  
* The filing deadline is 9 months after death, unless an extension is granted.  
* The U.S. estate tax applies only to the U.S. portion of the estate; the Brazilian apartment is excluded unless it is inherited by a U.S. heir, in which case that heir would face Brazilian tax and forced‑heirship rules.

answer_raw:
Your Brazilian apartment will **automatically become part of your estate** when you die in Brazil, and the ownership is transferred to your heirs retroactively under **Art. 1.784** of the Civil Code [1].  
The inheritance rules that follow are the same that apply to Brazilian citizens: at least **50 %** of the estate is a **reserved portion** that must go to legal heirs, while the remaining **disposable portion** can be distributed freely.  Inheritance tax (ITCMD) can reach up to **8 %** of the value of the inherited assets [2].

U.S. bank accounts, on the other hand, are governed by U.S. estate‑tax rules.  If the total value of your U.S.‑situated assets exceeds **$60 000**, your estate must file **Form 706‑NA** within nine months of death, unless an extension is granted [7][8].  The U.S. estate tax applies only to U.S. assets; Brazilian property is excluded from that calculation.

Because Brazilian inheritance law applies regardless of the heir’s citizenship, any U.S. heir who receives the apartment will be subject to the Brazilian forced‑heirship rules and the up‑to‑8 % tax.  The U.S. estate tax does not affect the Brazilian property, and vice versa.

To avoid cross‑border complications, consider preparing a Brazilian will (or trust) for the apartment and a separate U.S. will or trust for the U.S. accounts, each following its own jurisdiction’s rules.
